s.note: Whipped quark and butter with paprika, caraway, capers and chives, with dark rye, radishes and gherkins
s.how: Beat 250g quark with 100g soft butter until smooth. Stir in 1 tbsp sweet paprika, 1 tsp crushed caraway seeds, 1 tsp mustard, 1 tbsp chopped capers, 1 finely chopped eschalot, 2 tbsp chopped chives and a good pinch of salt. Chill for 30 minutes so it firms and turns a deep orange. Pile into a bowl, dust with more paprika and serve with sliced dark rye, halved radishes and gherkins.

s.n: Nonnberg Abbey pretzels with sweet mustard
s.note: Soft baked pretzels with a dark chewy crust and salt flakes, with sweet mustard for dipping
s.how: Mix 500g bread flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tsp sugar, 1 1/2 tsp salt, 40g soft butter and 300ml warm water, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Cover and prove for 1 hour until doubled. Cut into 8 pieces, roll each into a 50cm rope, thin at the ends, and twist into pretzels. Rest on lined trays for 10 minutes. Bring 2 litres of water to a simmer with 4 tbsp bicarbonate of soda and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds, then lift back onto the trays. Sprinkle with salt flakes, slash the thick part and bake at 220C for 15 minutes until deep brown. Serve warm with sweet mustard.

s.note: Browned cheese kranskys with caraway sauerkraut, horseradish cream, hot mustard and cornichons
s.how: Warm 400g sauerkraut in a small pan with 1 tsp caraway seeds and a splash of water for 10 minutes. Score 8 cheese kranskys and brown them in 1 tbsp oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until the cheese starts to bubble out. Slice on an angle and pile on a board with the sauerkraut, 2 tbsp horseradish cream, 4 tbsp hot mustard and a handful of cornichons.

m.note: Beef rump cap simmered with root vegetables in its own broth, apple horseradish, chive sauce and buttered potatoes
m.how: Char 1 halved brown onion cut side down in a dry pan until black. Put a 1.5kg beef rump cap in a large pot, cover with 3 litres of cold water, bring to a simmer and skim. Add the onion, 2 carrots, 1 leek, a quarter of a celeriac, 2 bay leaves, 10 peppercorns and 2 tsp salt and simmer very gently, lid ajar, for 2 1/2 hours until tender. Meanwhile boil 800g waxy potatoes until just tender, slice thickly and fry in 50g butter until golden, then toss with parsley. Grate 2 green apples into 3 tbsp horseradish cream and the juice of half a lemon. Mix 200g sour cream, 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 tsp white wine vinegar and a bunch of chopped chives. Rest the beef in the broth for 10 minutes, slice across the grain and serve in shallow bowls with a ladle of broth, the potatoes and both sauces.

w.note: Three golden peaks of baked vanilla and lemon meringue souffle over warm raspberries, dusted with icing sugar
w.how: Heat the oven to 200C. Butter a 25cm oval baking dish with 30g butter, scatter in 200g frozen raspberries and 2 tbsp caster sugar, pour in 150ml milk with 1/2 tsp vanilla and warm in the oven for 5 minutes. Whisk 6 egg whites with a pinch of salt to soft peaks, then add 80g caster sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk until stiff and glossy. Mix 4 egg yolks with the zest of half a lemon and 1/2 tsp vanilla, then fold through the whites with 30g sifted plain flour. Pile into three tall peaks in the dish with a spatula and bake for 12 to 13 minutes until golden outside and soft in the middle. Dust with icing sugar and take it straight to the table.

d.note: Elderflower cordial, cloudy apple and lemon over ice with mint, topped with soda
d.how: Mix 200ml elderflower cordial, 400ml cloudy apple juice and the juice of 2 lemons in a jug and chill. Bruise a handful of mint leaves and drop them in. Fill 4 tall glasses with ice, pour in the elderflower mix and top with 1 litre of soda water. Stir gently and garnish with a lemon wheel and a mint sprig.
